title: Barclays lowers 2027 S&P 500 target as tighter financial conditions weigh
html:
Barclays on Monday trimmed its 2027 year-end target for the benchmark S&P 500 index to 8,700 from 8,800, saying higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions limit scope for valuation expansion.

Earnings growth is likely to slow next year due to tougher year-on-year comparisons, but strong demand, resilient pricing power and continued heavy investment should help sustain the current profit growth cycle, Barclays said.

The brokerage expects S&P 500 earnings per share of US$377 in 2026 and US$434 in 2027, with profits growing 15 per cent in 2027 from a year earlier.

Barclays said: “2027 hinges on earnings, and earnings hinge on chips.” It estimates semiconductor and hardware firms would drive at least 50 per cent of S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 and 2028, underscoring growing concentration risk.

The AI-driven rally that has fuelled much of the index’s advance this year has recently faced headwinds from higher borrowing costs, fears of slower growth after the Democrats’ midterm election victory and turmoil surrounding Nvidia’s leadership transition.

In its bull-case scenario, Barclays expects the S&P 500 to reach 9,400 by the end of 2027, while its bear-case forecast sees the index falling to 6,450.

Meanwhile, Barclays upgraded the U.S. healthcare sector to “positive” from “neutral,” saying it was well positioned to deliver double-digit earnings growth, supported by strong demand trends and improving earnings revisions.

The brokerage downgraded the U.S. communication services sector to “neutral” citing concentration risks and cut the US materials sector to “negative” on fading growth tailwinds.
summary: Expects S&P 500 earnings per share of US$377 in 2026 and US$434 in 2027
